title: Joining by order id
text: The transition `fork` mints a fresh name for each `order` and writes it into both tokens it produces, and `ship` has a match on `paid` and `picked`, so it joins a payment and a pick only when they carry the same name. Without the match, two orders in flight could be shipped with each other's payment.

steps.text: The first order gets the fresh name A: one request in `payReq` and one in `pickReq`, both carrying A.
The second order gets B. Minted names never repeat within a run.
The payment of A completes: `paid` holds A.
Actions run concurrently, and the pick of B completes before the pick of A: `picked` holds B. Both places are marked, yet no name is in both, so `ship` is not enabled.
The pick of A completes. A is now in `paid` and in `picked`.
The transition `ship` joins the two A tokens. Had two names been eligible, it would take the one with the oldest token, ties broken by name, the same in every language.
The transition `ship` joins the two B tokens. Every order shipped with its own payment.
